Re:Source is an AI-assisted reuse marketplace for non-structural renovation leftovers. Owners upload a photo and confirm an AI-generated listing draft. Finders describe a project; Re:Source converts it into requirements, filters real inventory, performs deterministic quantity, area and price calculations, and explains what fits, what is missing and what to ask before pickup.
Use the mosaic tabletop scenario as the opening example.

Opportunity: usable leftovers are lost because supply is difficult to describe and demand is expressed as projects rather than product keywords.
Difference: Re:Source connects a project brief to structured inventory using transparent calculations and explicit uncertainty.
USP: every recommendation cites confirmed listing facts, shows coverage and gaps, and keeps AI suggestions separate from owner-confirmed data.

Implemented in the prototype: guided project brief; structured inventory browsing; deterministic match, quantity, area and price calculations; evidence and uncertainty states; saved project plan; manual listing; simulated pickup; responsive desktop/mobile experience; clear AI availability and fallback states.
Planned for submission-grade live demo: Gemini photo-to-draft, brief-to-requirements and evidence-backed match explanation; Firebase persistence, anonymous authentication and App Check; public deployment.
Label implemented and planned features separately in the deck.

Owner flow: photograph leftover → review AI suggestions → correct details → publish.
Finder flow: describe project → review extracted requirements → inspect ranked matches → see calculations and uncertainty → save plan → simulate pickup.
Signature demo: a renter needs a small mosaic tabletop; Re:Source identifies suitable tile leftovers, calculates coverage and cost, flags missing details and saves the plan.
Record the full owner and finder journeys.
Use one early wireframe beside the final interface to show how the experience evolved from catalogue browsing into a guided conversation with progressive disclosure.

Target flow: React/Vite/shadcn UI → Firebase Hosting → anonymous Firebase Authentication + App Check → Firestore for listings/projects → Firebase AI Logic → Gemini Developer API. Client-side image resizing is used before AI analysis. Deterministic application code handles quantity, area and price calculations; AI produces structured suggestions and explanations. No Cloud Storage, Cloud Functions, Cloud Run or Vertex AI are planned under the no-billing constraint.
Verify Firebase project, model access and quotas before presenting as deployed.

Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite 8, Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui.
App services planned: Firebase Hosting, Firestore, anonymous Authentication and App Check.
AI planned: Firebase AI Logic with the Gemini Developer API.
Testing: Vitest plus browser-based journey checks.
Design principle: AI proposes; users confirm; calculations remain deterministic.
Update once the final deployment stack is confirmed.

Prototype target: ₹0 paid usage. The proposed design uses unbilled Firebase Spark services and free-tier Gemini Developer API access through Firebase AI Logic. This is a design constraint, not a guarantee of capacity: model availability, quotas and event rules must be verified before submission.
